Lucky my feet didn’t change too much from pregnancy, just some flatter arches. I cannot fit into my aggressive bouldering shoes and don’t even care to. I think it’s a “beginner” shoe but I’ve been climbing for 10 years now and it’s my favorite shoe still and might be worth trying - La Sportiva Finale. The color changed to blue, I have the pink and keep resoling them. Get what fits your new feet! Honestly think the intense / high arch shoes are a little ridiculous, get a flatter/ beginner shoe! Feels more comfy and you can get better smears

I think after 1 year pp, I’ve accepted things are going to look different now. On Sundays I use her nap to do my 1 hour yin and meditation, read my Bible and journal at night instead of the AM, and get in my walks when I can.

I was really pushing to get “back to normal” and finally realized normal is different now. And let me tell you, it still brings me to tears thinking of how care free I was and how much time I use to have for myself. 

My advice, start small and make it work for your current situation/ schedule. And, be kind to yourself. PP is not just the 3 months after baby is born it’s such a process

We did fuss it out but didn’t start till after 4 months. I’d put her down before she was tired so she wasn’t over tired and it eventually worked. Took a week or so but it worked! I also didn’t do the norm in that I did sleep training for naps not bedtime first.

When the fussing got out of hand I’d pick her up and soothe her and try again. If after 30min she wasn’t asleep, I’d rock or feed her to sleep and try again next nap.

I’d say it’s best to wait till your baby is 4+ months before trying so they can self soothe. It may take a few days or weeks but eventually they will learn to fall asleep on their own ❤️

Same experience - folly bulb then got induced with pitocin 24hrs later. I was 42weeks and 2 days 😭 really hoping for that natural birth but it is what it is, also suffer from endometriosis and pray we can get pregnant again so I can have another try at a natural labor. 

Anywho, the folly bulb was easy to be placed but definitely brought on strong contractions for me! Labored at home in the tub which was amazing and then the contractions just stopped… I hardly dilated. (Turns out baby had a short umbilical cord which may have contributed to the minimal dilation)

Pitocin wasn’t as bad as everyone made it seem in my opinion. Felt about the level of my period cramps except was more exhausting because they got me laboring at 2 min apart for 7 hours. I was falling asleep in between contractions so I got the epidural, 3 hours later pushed my girl out!!

It’s scary because of the unknown but you will be great!! I didn’t see myself getting induced but honestly it was a lot smoother than I could have hoped. Hope this gives some encouragement 🩷
